units.oracle: QA-owned BFS of REQ-TIECAP-3 plus closed-form usability and REQ-TIECAP-9 precedence, implemented in the test file without importing app.network or app.flisr helpers; seed and case count printed in the test output for the PR evidence.

questions.question: What is 'tie capacity'? The source says it is the 'rated capacity' (a static nameplate rating) but also says it arrives from the SCADA scan every 10 s (a live value, usually the alternate feeder's spare capacity). Which is it, and in which unit: kW (what the code uses today), kVA or A (feeders carry rating_amps)? If it is kVA or A, what power factor or voltage converts the load_kw load basis, and what p.u. base should the tolerance use?
questions.answer: Live value. 'Tie capacity' is the alternate feeder's spare capacity as delivered by the SCADA scan every 10 s, in kW on the same basis as load_kw. No unit conversion, no p.u. base; comparison tolerance is 0.5 kW. The 'rated capacity' wording in the source is loose and does not mean nameplate.

questions.question: When is a 10 s scan value 'late' (for example 20 s = 2 missed scans, or 30 s)? Inside that window, may the planner hold the last good value, or must it refuse any value older than one scan?
questions.answer: A value is late when it is older than 20 s (two missed scans). Inside 20 s the planner may use the last value only if its quality is GOOD. Older than 20 s, or any quality other than GOOD, is 'unknown' and must not be used.

questions.question: Today tie_capacity_kw is a bare dict[str, float] with no timestamp or quality. How should the value's timestamp and SCADA quality reach build_plan and POST /flisr/plan? May we extend the build_plan signature and the POST /flisr/plan body (an API change for the SCADA adapter), and who owns the adapter side?
questions.answer: Extend build_plan with tie_capacity: dict[str, TieCapacity] where TieCapacity carries kw, timestamp and quality (a Pydantic model in backend/app/models.py). Extend the POST /flisr/plan body the same way. Keep the legacy dict[str, float] accepted for one release and treat it as quality GOOD with timestamp now, with a deprecation note. The SCADA adapter side is owned by the integration team and is out of scope for this change.

questions.question: When transferred load exactly equals tie capacity, should the tie close or not? Is a safety margin or comparison tolerance needed, stated in kW and p.u.?
questions.answer: Equality closes: the tie may close when transferred load <= capacity. No additional safety margin; the only tolerance is the 0.5 kW comparison tolerance from Q-SPEC-1. No p.u. statement needed.

questions.question: The source says 'the plan must say so instead of restoring'. When one tie's capacity is unknown, is only that tie blocked (the lockout reclose and ties with known capacity still go ahead), or is the whole restoration refused (isolation-only / manual-action plan, or HTTP 409)? Must 'capacity unknown' also be a machine-readable RestorationPlan field, not only a free-text note?
questions.answer: Per tie. Only the tie with unknown capacity is blocked; isolation and ties with a known capacity proceed. 'Capacity unknown' must be machine-readable: RestorationPlan gains blocked_ties: list[BlockedTie{tie_id, reason in CAPACITY_UNKNOWN | CAPACITY_STALE | CAPACITY_INVALID | CAPACITY_EXCEEDED}] and an operator-readable note; HTTP 200, not 409.

questions.question: When load exceeds capacity, should the planner try a partial pick-up (open a downstream sectionalizer so the rest fits), or is skipping the tie the required outcome? Skipping is today's behaviour.
questions.answer: Skip the tie (today's behaviour) and record it in blocked_ties with reason CAPACITY_EXCEEDED. Partial pick-up is out of scope.

questions.question: When two or more ties pick up load from the same alternate feeder, is capacity per tie, or shared so that the sum of the transfers must fit? The shipped model has one tie, so the source does not settle this.
questions.answer: Per tie. Shared alternate-feeder capacity across several ties is out of scope; list it as a scope exclusion.

questions.question: The brief's layer map names backend/app/state_estimation.py and backend/app/main.py, but those files do not exist; the real files are state_estimator.py and api.py. The source also names locate_fault as the planner, but the capacity logic is in build_plan. Please confirm that build_plan plus api.py is the intended scope, and correct the repo contract's layer map.
questions.answer: Confirmed: scope is build_plan in backend/app/flisr.py plus backend/app/api.py (and models.py for the new types). The repo contract layer map has been corrected to state_estimator.py / api.py.

questions.question: What triggers CAPACITY_INVALID, and how are reasons assigned? (a) Which kw values are invalid: NaN, ±inf, negative? A negative spare capacity could be a real reading (alternate feeder already overloaded) or a bad value; with L=0 kW and C=-0.3 the tie would close unless negative values are invalid. (b) Does quality != GOOD give CAPACITY_UNKNOWN or CAPACITY_INVALID? (c) BlockedTie has one reason: when several conditions hold (e.g. stale + not GOOD + NaN), which is recorded? (d) A malformed HTTP entry (e.g. string kw, missing quality): reject the whole request with 422, or block only that tie with CAPACITY_INVALID and return 200?
questions.answer: CAPACITY_INVALID = kw is NaN, +/-inf, negative, or not a finite number, or the timestamp is unparseable/timezone-naive/future-dated (see Q-SPEC-10). A quality other than GOOD is CAPACITY_UNKNOWN (same as missing). Precedence when several apply, evaluate in this order and report the first: CAPACITY_INVALID, CAPACITY_UNKNOWN, CAPACITY_STALE, CAPACITY_EXCEEDED. Malformed HTTP input (wrong types, unknown fields) is rejected by request validation with HTTP 422 and never reaches the planner.

questions.question: What is the time reference for staleness? (a) Is t_eval the planner's UTC wall clock when build_plan starts, or an evaluation time supplied by the caller or injected? (b) A timestamp later than t_eval (clock skew): usable, stale, or invalid? Is any skew allowed? Without a rule a future-dated value looks fresh indefinitely. (c) A timezone-naive timestamp: reject, or interpret as UTC?
questions.answer: Time reference is the request's as_of field: a timezone-aware ISO-8601 UTC instant supplied by the caller; when absent the server uses UTC now and echoes the value it used in the response. Capacity timestamps must be timezone-aware; naive timestamps are CAPACITY_INVALID. A timestamp more than 2 s ahead of as_of is CAPACITY_INVALID. Age = as_of - timestamp.

questions.question: How does the legacy dict[str, float] coexist with the new form? (a) HTTP body: keep the legacy floats under tie_capacity_kw next to a new tie_capacity field, or one field that accepts either shape? (b) If both forms are supplied in one call, or for the same tie: refuse, new form wins, or something else? (c) Where does the 'deprecation note' go: RestorationPlan.notes (shown to operators), an HTTP Deprecation header, OpenAPI deprecated, a log line, or several?
questions.answer: The new body field tie_capacity (dict[str, TieCapacity]) and the legacy tie_capacity_kw are mutually exclusive; both present is HTTP 422. Legacy-only requests are treated as quality GOOD with timestamp = as_of and the response carries deprecations: ['tie_capacity_kw']. The deprecation note lives in the endpoint's OpenAPI description and in the docs page the Document stage produces; removal is a separate change after one release.

questions.question: Invalid as_of. Q-SPEC-10 only covers a missing as_of. What happens when the supplied as_of is (a) timezone-naive, (b) aware but with a non-UTC offset such as +02:00 (accept it as the same instant, or reject?), or (c) unparseable? The two options are: reject with HTTP 422, so no plan and not even isolation; or build the plan with isolation and block every candidate tie as CAPACITY_INVALID. (d) Should a supplied as_of be bounded against the server clock? Without a bound, a caller can back-date as_of so that stale capacity looks fresh, which bypasses the 20 s staleness rule.
questions.answer: (a) timezone-naive as_of: HTTP 422. (b) aware non-UTC offset: accept, normalise to the same UTC instant. (c) unparseable: HTTP 422. (d) yes, bounded: an as_of more than 60 s before or 2 s after the server clock is HTTP 422, so staleness cannot be bypassed by back-dating. 422 means no plan at all, which is acceptable because the request itself is malformed; the operator retries with a valid request.

questions.question: Unparseable capacity timestamp over HTTP. Q-SPEC-9 says an unparseable timestamp is CAPACITY_INVALID (per tie, HTTP 200) and that wrong types get HTTP 422 for the whole request. In JSON the timestamp is a string either way, so is a non-ISO-8601 string such as 'yesterday' (a) a per-tie CAPACITY_INVALID with HTTP 200, which means TieCapacity.timestamp must accept any string, or (b) a 422? And is a JSON number (Unix seconds) a wrong type (422) or accepted?
questions.answer: (b) 422. TieCapacity.timestamp is a strict timezone-aware ISO-8601 datetime field; a non-ISO string or a JSON number is a request-validation failure for the whole request. Per-tie CAPACITY_INVALID for timestamps therefore covers only well-formed values that fail the semantic rules (future-dated beyond 2 s). Q-SPEC-9 is amended to match.

questions.question: STD-ARCH-2 says one shared implementation of a threshold characteristic must be used by every consumer, including a test oracle, and that duplicates are a VIOLATION. STD-SAFETY-6 and spec section 4 / REQ-TIECAP-3 require an independent closed-form oracle that does not import app.flisr, so it has to restate L <= C + 0.5 kW, age > 20 s, age < -2 s and the INVALID>UNKNOWN>STALE>EXCEEDED precedence. Which rule governs the QA oracle? (a) STD-SAFETY-6 (proposed): the oracle restates the closed form with literals from the spec, and one test pins the models.py constants to the spec values; STD-ARCH-2 then applies only to production consumers. (b) STD-ARCH-2: the tests call flisr.tie_capacity_verdict, independence comes only from hand-computed boundary expectations, and the spec's oracle clause is amended. (c) Middle ground: the oracle imports the models.py constants only and restates the comparison and the precedence.
questions.answer: STD-SAFETY-6 governs the oracle: the QA/test oracle is an independent closed form that lives under backend/tests and must not import app.flisr or share its threshold code. STD-ARCH-2's one-shared-implementation rule applies to production consumers only (planner, endpoint, notes); record this as an explicit, scoped waiver in design section 6.3 citing both clauses, and keep the production threshold characteristic (tolerance, max age, max lead) in one shared module that every production consumer imports.

questions.question: A section with negative Section.load_kw (e.g. DG export) inside a candidate set whose total L is still >= 0 makes L understate the load the tie would actually carry (measured: spur -600 kW, C=1000 -> closes at L=890 kW while the non-negative loads total 1490 kW). Pick one: (a) refuse the plan with FlisrError when any candidate-section load_kw < 0 (recommended; REQ-TIECAP-3/21 scoped to non-negative section loads); (b) use gross L = sum(max(load_kw, 0)) (changes the spec's L definition); (c) keep REQ-TIECAP-3 literal and accept the residual risk; (d) declare negative loads out of scope (model-team rule, no runtime check).
questions.answer: A negative, NaN or infinite section load is invalid model data, not a load to net off. build_plan refuses the whole plan (FlisrError, HTTP 409, lockout stays open) when any candidate section's load_kw is not a finite non-negative number; L is otherwise the plain sum. This is covered by the out-of-range precondition and needs no change to REQ-TIECAP-3/21; record it in the design as a stated precondition and add a test vector.

questions.question: Draft PR #13 (DEF-FLISR-7) holds a candidate tie open with a note and no blocked_ties entry, which contradicts REQ-TIECAP-21 ('every candidate tie not closed appears exactly once in blocked_ties'). Pick one: (a) ties held open by the DEF-FLISR-7 guard are not candidate ties for REQ-TIECAP-11/18/21; the guard runs before L and the verdict (recommended); (b) add a fifth BlockedTie reason, e.g. BACKFEED_FAULTED_SECTION, ahead of CAPACITY_INVALID (changes Q-SPEC-5 enum, REQ-TIECAP-9/11); (c) fix a merge order and let the second change amend its own requirements.

artifacts.specification:
# Specification: FLISR restoration respects tie-switch capacity

Run `feature-tie-capacity`, stage SPECIFY, attempt 1. Target repo `tedfoley-cog/adms-test-automation-demo` @ `5f6b471` (main).

## 1. Classification (STD-REQ-6, STD-SAFETY-1)
**Safety-critical** (IEC 61508-3 context). The change decides whether a tie switch is closed onto field load during FLISR restoration. Every unit derived from this specification inherits this classification. `backend/app/flisr.py` is a protected path: two human reviewers before merge (STD-GOV-6).

## 2. Where the behaviour lives today (repo evidence)
- The capacity decision is in `backend/app/flisr.py::build_plan` (lines 64-128), not in `locate_fault`. `locate_fault` (lines 24-35) only picks the faulted section and never reads capacity.
- Capacity input: `build_plan(..., tie_capacity_kw: dict[str, float] | None)`. Over HTTP it is `FlisrRequest.tie_capacity_kw: dict[str, float] = {}` in `backend/app/api.py` (lines 15-18). No timestamp, quality flag or source field exists.
- Load transferred by a tie = sum of `Section.load_kw` (static model value, kW) over the nodes the tie would pick up (`_nodes_restored_by` + `network.load_on_nodes`).
- Rule today: `available = tie_capacity_kw.get(switch.mrid, 0.0)`; the tie closes when `transferred <= available`, otherwise it is skipped with a note.

Current behaviour, observed on the shipped `FDR-1201` model with `CB-1201.open = True` (fault at SEC-1201-03, tie `TIE-1201-1405` would pick up 1490 kW / 341 customers):

| Capacity input for TIE-1201-1405 | Tie closed? | Plan note | Conforms to source? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2000 kW | yes, 1490 kW transferred | none | yes |
| 1920 kW | yes | none | yes |
| -5 kW | no | "skipped: 1490 kW exceeds -5 kW available capacity" | no: an invalid value is reported as a real capacity |
| missing | no | "skipped: 1490 kW exceeds 0 kW available capacity" | no: missing is treated as 0 kW (implicit zero, STD-REQ-3) and the plan does not say capacity is unknown |
| missing, candidate load 0 kW | **yes** | none | **no: closes a tie whose capacity is unknown** |
| NaN | **yes, 1490 kW transferred** | none | **no: `1490 > nan` is False, so an invalid value restores** |
| +inf | **yes** | none | no: a non-finite value is accepted as capacity |

Pydantic accepts `-1` and `NaN` in `FlisrRequest.tie_capacity_kw` without error.

## 3. Requirements
Inputs: feeder model, lockout switch mRID, per-tie capacity value. Outputs: `RestorationPlan.restoration`, `.notes`, `.customers_restored`, `.customers_remaining`, `.transferred_load_kw`.

**REQ-FLISR-001 (capacity bound).** For every tie switch `T` that `build_plan` puts in `plan.restoration` with action `close`, the load transferred through `T` (kW, sum of `load_kw` of the sections `T` would pick up after isolation) shall be less than or equal to the known capacity of `T` (kW), subject to the limit rule in REQ-FLISR-002.
- Unit: kW (pending Q-SPEC-1). Range: finite, >= 0. 
- Verification: test plus a seeded invariant (>= 500 cases, STD-SAFETY-5). Oracle: see section 5.

**REQ-FLISR-002 (behaviour at the limit).** When transferred load equals the known capacity, the tie shall [close | not close] and the comparison shall use tolerance [X kW / X p.u.]. *Open: Q-SPEC-4.* Today the tie closes at equality with exact float comparison.
- Verification: boundary tests at capacity - delta, = capacity, + delta, with delta stated in kW and p.u. (STD-SAFETY-6).

**REQ-FLISR-003 (exceeds capacity).** When transferred load exceeds the known capacity of `T`, `build_plan` shall not close `T`; shall add a note naming `T`'s name, the transferred kW and the capacity kW; shall add the customers `T` would have picked up to `customers_remaining`; and shall add nothing for `T` to `customers_restored` or `transferred_load_kw`. Whether partial pick-up should be tried instead: *Q-SPEC-6.*
- Verification: test (characterization of the current note format plus the counters).

**REQ-FLISR-004 (unknown capacity: missing).** When no capacity value is supplied for a SCADA-controllable tie `T` that has candidate nodes, `build_plan` shall refuse to close `T` (whatever the candidate load, including 0 kW) and shall add a note that names `T` and says its capacity is unknown. It shall not report a numeric capacity for `T`, and shall not treat the missing value as 0 kW. Counters as in REQ-FLISR-003. Whether the rest of the plan still proceeds: *Q-SPEC-5.*
- Handling: **refuse** (STD-REQ-3).
- Verification: tests for missing with candidate load > 0 and with candidate load = 0 kW (the second fails today).

**REQ-FLISR-005 (unknown capacity: invalid).** A capacity value that is NaN, +/-inf or negative shall be treated as unknown: REQ-FLISR-004 applies, and the note shall say the value was invalid. Zero is a valid, known capacity: any candidate load > 0 kW exceeds it (REQ-FLISR-003).
- Handling: **refuse + flag quality** in the note.
- Verification: tests for NaN, +inf, -inf, -5 kW and 0 kW. NaN and +inf fail today.

**REQ-FLISR-006 (unknown capacity: stale / bad quality).** Capacity telemetry arrives from the SCADA scan every 10 s. A capacity value older than [N s] at plan time, or flagged bad quality by SCADA, shall be treated as unknown (REQ-FLISR-004), with the note giving the age or quality. Whether a hold-last-value window is allowed: *Q-SPEC-2.* How age and quality reach `build_plan` / `POST /flisr/plan` (today only a bare float exists): *Q-SPEC-3.*
- Handling: refuse (hold-last-value only if Q-SPEC-2 allows it).
- Verification: tests with value age at limit - 1 s, = limit, limit + 1 s; bad-quality flag.

**REQ-FLISR-007 (capacity in the API).** `POST /flisr/plan` shall accept the capacity inputs needed by REQ-FLISR-004..006 and shall return the plan (HTTP 200) with the unknown-capacity note. It shall not answer 422 or 409 just because one tie's capacity is unknown, unless Q-SPEC-5 decides the whole plan is refused.
- Verification: API test through `fastapi.testclient` with missing, NaN (if the JSON transport allows it) and negative values.

**REQ-FLISR-008 (unchanged behaviour).** With every tie capacity known, valid, fresh and not exceeded, `build_plan` shall give the same plan as `main@5f6b471`: every isolation step, restoration step and order, the counters and the notes. This includes the existing test `test_build_plan_isolates_and_restores_tail` (2000 kW, 341 customers restored).
- Verification: characterization tests (`@pytest.mark.characterization`) written before any code change (STD-SAFETY-2).

**REQ-FLISR-009 (defects reproduced first).** Before the fix, DEF-FLISR-001..003 shall each have a failing test that states the defect in operational terms (STD-SAFETY-3).

### Defects found while specifying
- **DEF-FLISR-001**: a NaN capacity closes the tie and transfers 1490 kW (`transferred > available` is False for NaN). Violates REQ-FLISR-001 and 005.
- **DEF-FLISR-002**: a missing capacity defaults to 0.0 kW. The plan reports "0 kW available capacity" instead of "unknown", and the tie closes when the candidate load is 0 kW. Violates REQ-FLISR-004 and STD-REQ-3.
- **DEF-FLISR-003**: +inf and negative capacities are accepted as real values (+inf restores; -5 kW is reported as a capacity). Violates REQ-FLISR-005.

## 4. Safety invariant (STD-SAFETY-5)
**INV-1**: For every plan, each tie in `plan.restoration` with action `close` has a known, valid, fresh capacity C and an independently computed transferred load L with L <= C (+ the tolerance from Q-SPEC-4). No tie whose capacity is missing, invalid or stale is ever closed.
Demonstrated over at least 500 seeded `random` cases: radial and branched feeders with 1-3 tie switches, fault-indicator patterns, section loads 0-3000 kW (including 0), and capacity inputs drawn from {missing, NaN, +/-inf, negative, 0, below L, = L, above L}. No new dependencies.

## 5. Verification method and independent oracle (STD-REQ-5, STD-SAFETY-6)
| Req | Method | Oracle |
|---|---|---|
| REQ-FLISR-001, 002 | test + seeded invariant | Closed-form oracle written in the test: BFS over the test-built topology with isolation switches open and the tie closed, minus nodes reachable from the own source; L = sum of section `load_kw`. It does not call `_nodes_restored_by`, `network.energised_nodes` or `network.load_on_nodes`. Tolerance stated in kW and in p.u. of the tie capacity (base per Q-SPEC-1). |
| REQ-FLISR-003 | test | Hand-computed expected note and counters for FDR-1201. |
| REQ-FLISR-004, 005, 006 | test | Expected outcome tables (section 2 and the requirement text); for missing/invalid/stale, the expected result is "not closed + unknown-capacity note". |
| REQ-FLISR-007 | test (API) | HTTP status + plan body. |
| REQ-FLISR-008 | characterization test | Plans recorded from `main@5f6b471`. |
| REQ-FLISR-009 | test (fails before the fix) | Failure output kept for the PR. |
| INV-1 | analysis/demonstration over >= 500 seeded cases | Same BFS oracle as REQ-FLISR-001. |

## 6. Scope exclusions (STD-REQ-7)
- `locate_fault` fault location logic (no capacity involvement; see Q-SPEC-8).
- The known defect where `_isolation_switches` skips tie switches (back-feed of a section next to a tie). Separate change.
- Real-time measured load on the transferred sections: the static `Section.load_kw` stays the load basis unless Q-SPEC-1 decides otherwise.
- The SCADA scan adapter / ICCP ingest itself. This change specifies only what `build_plan` and `POST /flisr/plan` do with the value they receive.
- Console (`console/**`) UI changes, AGC, state estimation, firmware, legacy Habitat tasks.
- Partial pick-up / load shedding to fit a tie's capacity (pending Q-SPEC-6; excluded unless the answer brings it in).
- Thermal, voltage-drop or protection-coordination checks on the alternate feeder other than the single capacity number.

## 7. Open questions (STD-REQ-4)
- **Q-SPEC-1** (blocks REQ-FLISR-001, 002, 003, INV-1): What quantity is "tie capacity"? The source says "rated capacity" (a static nameplate rating), yet says it comes from the SCADA scan every 10 s (a live value, normally the alternate feeder's spare capacity). Which is it, and in which unit: kW (as the code uses today), kVA or A (feeders carry `rating_amps`)? If kVA or A, what power factor / voltage base converts the `load_kw` load basis? What p.u. base should the tolerance use?
- **Q-SPEC-2** (blocks REQ-FLISR-006): After what age is a 10 s scan value "late" (for example 2 missed scans = 20 s, or 30 s)? Inside that window, may the last good value be held (hold-last-value), or must any value older than one scan be refused?
- **Q-SPEC-3** (blocks REQ-FLISR-006, 007): How do value timestamp and SCADA quality reach the planner? Today `tie_capacity_kw` is a bare `dict[str, float]` with no time or quality. Is it acceptable to extend the `build_plan` signature and the `POST /flisr/plan` body (an API change for the SCADA adapter), and who owns the adapter side?
- **Q-SPEC-4** (blocks REQ-FLISR-002, INV-1): At exactly `transferred == capacity`, close or not? Is a safety margin or comparison tolerance needed (in kW and p.u.)?
- **Q-SPEC-5** (blocks REQ-FLISR-004, 007): "The plan must say so instead of restoring." When one tie's capacity is unknown, does that block only that tie (the lockout reclose and other ties with known capacity still go ahead), or the whole restoration (plan returns isolation only / manual action, or the API answers 409)? Should "capacity unknown" also be a machine-readable field in `RestorationPlan`, not only a free-text note?
- **Q-SPEC-6** (blocks REQ-FLISR-003): When load exceeds capacity, should the planner try partial pick-up (open a downstream sectionalizer so the rest fits), or is skipping the tie (today's behaviour) the required outcome?
- **Q-SPEC-7** (blocks REQ-FLISR-001, INV-1): When two or more ties pick up load from the same alternate feeder, is capacity per tie or shared, so the sum of transfers must fit? The shipped model has one tie, so the source does not settle it.
- **Q-SPEC-8** (non-blocking for the spec text; blocks DESIGN/ARCHITECT): The brief's layer map names `backend/app/state_estimation.py` and `backend/app/main.py`, which do not exist (the real files are `state_estimator.py` and `api.py`). The source names `locate_fault` as the planner, but the capacity logic is in `build_plan`. Please confirm `build_plan` + `api.py` is the intended scope and correct the repo contract's layer map.

## 8. Notes for later stages
- `ruff check backend tools` already fails on `main` (UP017 in `tools/build_coverage_report.py:183`), before any change from this run. Later stages should not count it as a regression or fix it as drive-by scope.
- To exercise `build_plan` on the shipped model, set `CB-1201.open = True`: no lockout is open in `feeder_model.json`, so `/flisr/plan` returns 409 otherwise.

# Specification — FLISR restoration respects tie-switch capacity

Run: `feature-tie-capacity` · Stage: SPECIFY · Attempt: 2 · Status: **BLOCKED** (open questions Q-SPEC-9, Q-SPEC-10, Q-SPEC-11)

## 0. Source, inputs and classification

- Source: change request "respect tie-switch capacity during FLISR restoration" plus human answers Q-SPEC-1..Q-SPEC-8 (ops-lead-standin).
- Safety classification (STD-REQ-6): **safety-critical** (IEC 61508-3 context). The change alters which tie switches FLISR commands closed. Every unit derived from this specification inherits the classification. `backend/app/flisr.py` is a protected path and needs two human reviewers (STD-GOV-6, STD-SAFETY-1).
- Scope (Q-SPEC-8): `build_plan` in `backend/app/flisr.py`, `POST /flisr/plan` in `backend/app/api.py`, and new types in `backend/app/models.py`.

### Current behaviour (baseline, `main` @ 5f6b471)

- `build_plan(feeder, lockout_switch_mrid, tie_capacity_kw: dict[str, float] | None)`. A tie with no entry reads as `0.0` kW (`flisr.py:98`, `tie_capacity_kw.get(switch.mrid, 0.0)`). That is an implicit "treat as zero", which STD-REQ-3 forbids.
- A tie is skipped when `transferred > available` (strict). Equality closes. There is no tolerance.
- On the shipped model with `CB-1201` open and no capacity supplied, the plan isolates `SEC-1201-03` (opens `SEC-SW-1201-1` and `REC-1201-2`), re-closes `CB-1201` and skips `TIE-1201-1405` with the note `"Hollow Creek tie to 1405 skipped: 1490 kW exceeds 0 kW available capacity"`. The results are `customers_remaining = 437` and `customers_restored = 0`.
- There is no timestamp, no quality and no machine-readable reason for a skipped tie.

### Definitions

- **Tie**: a `Switch` with `kind == tie` and `scada_controllable == True` for which `_nodes_restored_by` returns a non-empty candidate node set. Other ties are out of scope (see §3). Today they are skipped silently, and that does not change.
- **L (transferred load)**: the sum of `Section.load_kw` over the sections whose `to_node` is in the tie's candidate node set. Unit kW. Range L ≥ 0.
- **C (tie capacity)**: the alternate feeder's spare capacity as delivered by the SCADA scan every 10 s. Unit kW, on the same basis as `load_kw`. No unit conversion and no per-unit base (Q-SPEC-1). It is not a nameplate rating.
- **Tolerance τ**: 0.5 kW. This is the only tolerance and no other safety margin applies (Q-SPEC-1, Q-SPEC-4). Per-unit statement waived by human answer Q-SPEC-4.
- **t_eval**: the instant against which a capacity value's age is judged. Its source is open (Q-SPEC-10).
- **age**: `t_eval − TieCapacity.timestamp`, in seconds.
- **Usable capacity**: an entry that is present, has `quality == "GOOD"` and `age ≤ 20 s` (Q-SPEC-2), and is not invalid (definition open, Q-SPEC-9).

Value validity is covered by REQ-TIECAP-8. | Test: construction and validation unit tests; inspection of `models.py`. | — |

The body field shape, what happens when both forms are supplied, and where the deprecation note goes are open. | legacy map → same decisions as REQ-TIECAP-3..12 | A tie missing from the legacy map → CAPACITY_UNKNOWN (REQ-TIECAP-5). ### Intended behaviour changes (blast radius)

1. A tie with no capacity entry used to be skipped with a "0 kW available" note. It is now blocked with reason CAPACITY_UNKNOWN (REQ-TIECAP-5). The step and the accounting are the same; the note text and `blocked_ties` are new.
2. `C < L ≤ C + 0.5 kW` used to skip the tie and now closes it (REQ-TIECAP-3, Q-SPEC-1/Q-SPEC-4). This is the **only** change that makes the planner more permissive. Reviewers should confirm it was intended.
3. A value that is stale or not GOOD used to be impossible to express. It now blocks the tie.
4. The `RestorationPlan` schema gains `blocked_ties`, an additive field.

## 2. Open questions (STD-REQ-4) — not resolved by assumption

- **Q-SPEC-9: when CAPACITY_INVALID applies, which reason a non-GOOD quality gets, and precedence.** (a) Which `kw` values are invalid: NaN, ±inf, negative? A negative spare capacity could be a real reading (the alternate feeder is already overloaded) or a bad one. With `L = 0 kW` candidate sections and `C = −0.3`, REQ-TIECAP-3 would close the tie unless negative values are invalid. (b) Does `quality != GOOD` give CAPACITY_UNKNOWN (Q-SPEC-2 calls it "unknown") or CAPACITY_INVALID? (c) `BlockedTie` carries one reason. When several conditions hold (for example stale and not GOOD and NaN), which reason is recorded? (d) A structurally malformed entry in the HTTP body (for example a string `kw` or a missing `quality`): reject the whole request with 422, or block only that tie with CAPACITY_INVALID and return 200? Blocks: REQ-TIECAP-7, REQ-TIECAP-8, REQ-TIECAP-13 (malformed input only), REQ-TIECAP-14 (legacy validity), REQ-TIECAP-17.
- **Q-SPEC-10: time reference.** (a) Is t_eval the planner's own wall clock (UTC) when `build_plan` starts, or an evaluation time supplied by the caller or injected? (b) A timestamp later than t_eval (clock skew between the SCADA front end and the planner): usable, stale, or invalid? Is any skew allowed? Without a rule, a future-dated value would look fresh indefinitely. (c) A timezone-naive timestamp: reject, or interpret as UTC? Blocks: REQ-TIECAP-6, REQ-TIECAP-16, REQ-TIECAP-17.
- **Q-SPEC-11: legacy format alongside the new one.** (a) HTTP body: keep the legacy floats under `tie_capacity_kw` next to the new `tie_capacity`, or have one field accept either shape? (b) If both forms are supplied in one call, or for the same tie: refuse, let the new form win, or something else? (c) Where does the "deprecation note" go: `RestorationPlan.notes` (shown to operators), an HTTP `Deprecation` header, OpenAPI `deprecated`, a log line, or several of these? Blocks: REQ-TIECAP-14.

## 3. Scope exclusions (STD-REQ-7)

- The SCADA adapter and telemetry ingestion: scan scheduling, quality mapping and timestamping (integration team, Q-SPEC-3).
- Spare capacity on one alternate feeder shared by several ties (Q-SPEC-7). Each tie is checked independently.
- Partial pick-up or load shedding to fit within capacity (Q-SPEC-6).
- Nameplate or thermal rating of the tie switch, unit conversion, per-unit bases, and any safety margin beyond τ = 0.5 kW (Q-SPEC-1, Q-SPEC-4).
- Removing the legacy `dict[str, float]` input (a later release).
- `locate_fault` and fault-location logic (open PRs #8 and #11). `_isolation_switches` and DEF-FLISR-7 (a tie that is an isolation point back-feeds the faulted section) are a separate defect run. This change shall not fix or mask DEF-FLISR-7.
- Ties that are not SCADA-controllable, and ties with an empty candidate node set. Both are skipped silently as today and are not listed in `blocked_ties`.
- `console/**`. The console does not call `/flisr/plan` today. `state_estimator.py`, `agc.py`, `savecase.py`, `firmware/**` and `legacy/**` are also out of scope.

- The independent oracle for the close/block decision is a QA-owned BFS over the test topology plus the closed-form checks `L ≤ C + 0.5`, `age > 20` and `quality == "GOOD"`. It must not import `app.network` or `app.flisr` helpers.

- Tool classification (STD-SAFETY-7) is the assessor's finding. The specification takes no tool-certification credit.

# Specification — FLISR restoration respects tie-switch capacity

Run: `feature-tie-capacity` · Stage: SPECIFY · Attempt: 3 · Status: **BLOCKED** (open questions Q-SPEC-12, Q-SPEC-13; every other requirement is complete)

## 0. Source, inputs and classification

- Source: change request "respect tie-switch capacity during FLISR restoration", plus human answers Q-SPEC-1..Q-SPEC-11 (ops-lead-standin, recorded gate actions).
- Safety classification (STD-REQ-6): **safety-critical** (IEC 61508-3 context). The change alters which tie switches FLISR commands closed. Every unit derived from this specification inherits the classification. `backend/app/flisr.py` is a protected path: two human reviewers (STD-GOV-6, STD-SAFETY-1).
- Scope (Q-SPEC-8): `build_plan` in `backend/app/flisr.py`; `POST /flisr/plan` in `backend/app/api.py`; new types in `backend/app/models.py`.

### Current behaviour (baseline, `main` @ 5f6b471, re-measured this attempt)

- `build_plan(feeder, lockout_switch_mrid, tie_capacity_kw: dict[str, float] | None)`. A tie with no entry reads as `0.0` kW (`flisr.py:98`, `tie_capacity_kw.get(switch.mrid, 0.0)`): an implicit "treat as zero", forbidden by STD-REQ-3.
- A tie is skipped when `transferred > available` (strict), so equality closes; there is no tolerance.
- Shipped model, `CB-1201` open: isolation opens `SEC-SW-1201-1` and `REC-1201-2`; restoration re-closes `CB-1201`. Tie `TIE-1201-1405` has L = 1490 kW.
  - no capacity → tie skipped, note `"Hollow Creek tie to 1405 skipped: 1490 kW exceeds 0 kW available capacity"`, `customers_restored = 0`, `customers_remaining = 437`, `transferred_load_kw = 0.0`.
  - C = 1490.0 → tie closed, `customers_restored = 341`, `customers_remaining = 96`, `transferred_load_kw = 1490.0`, no notes.
  - C = 1489.9 → tie skipped (note says "exceeds 1490 kW", rounding hides the 0.1 kW).
- HTTP today (`FlisrRequest`, Pydantic lax mode, extra fields ignored): a JSON `NaN` capacity is accepted, a string `"2000"` is coerced to 2000.0, and an unknown body field is silently ignored. All three reach the planner.
- No timestamp, no quality, no machine-readable reason for a skipped tie.

### Definitions

- **Candidate tie**: a `Switch` with `kind == tie` and `scada_controllable == True` for which `_nodes_restored_by` returns a non-empty node set. Other ties are skipped silently, as today (§3).
- **L (transferred load)**: sum of `Section.load_kw` over sections whose `to_node` is in the candidate node set. Unit kW; range L ≥ 0.
- **C (tie capacity)**: `TieCapacity.kw` — the alternate feeder's spare capacity as delivered by the SCADA scan every 10 s, kW on the same basis as `load_kw`. No unit conversion, no per-unit base, not nameplate (Q-SPEC-1).
- **τ (tolerance)**: 0.5 kW, the only tolerance; no additional safety margin (Q-SPEC-1, Q-SPEC-4). Per-unit statement waived by Q-SPEC-4.
- **as_of**: the evaluation instant. The request's `as_of` (timezone-aware ISO-8601 UTC instant supplied by the caller); when absent, the server's UTC now (Q-SPEC-10).
- **age**: `as_of − TieCapacity.timestamp`, in seconds (Q-SPEC-10). Negative when the timestamp is ahead of as_of.
- **Usable capacity**: an entry that is present, valid (REQ-TIECAP-8), `quality == "GOOD"` and `age ≤ 20 s` (Q-SPEC-2).
- **Present** (HTTP body field): the key appears in the JSON body, whatever its value.

# Specification — FLISR restoration respects tie-switch capacity

Run: `feature-tie-capacity` · Stage: SPECIFY · Attempt: 4 · Status: **COMPLETE** (no open questions; Q-SPEC-1..Q-SPEC-13 answered)

## 0. Source, inputs and classification

- Source: change request "respect tie-switch capacity during FLISR restoration", plus human answers Q-SPEC-1..Q-SPEC-13 (ops-lead-standin, recorded gate actions). Q-SPEC-13 amends Q-SPEC-9 and Q-SPEC-10: a timezone-naive or unparseable capacity timestamp is a request-validation failure, not a per-tie CAPACITY_INVALID.
- Safety classification (STD-REQ-6): **safety-critical** (IEC 61508-3 context). The change alters which tie switches FLISR commands closed. Every unit derived from this specification inherits the classification. `backend/app/flisr.py` is a protected path: two human reviewers (STD-GOV-6, STD-SAFETY-1).
- Scope (Q-SPEC-8): `build_plan` in `backend/app/flisr.py`; `POST /flisr/plan` in `backend/app/api.py`; new types in `backend/app/models.py`.

### Current behaviour (baseline, `main` @ 5f6b471, re-measured this attempt; `pytest backend -q` 2 passed)

- `build_plan(feeder, lockout_switch_mrid, tie_capacity_kw: dict[str, float] | None)`. A tie with no entry reads as `0.0` kW (`flisr.py:98`, `tie_capacity_kw.get(switch.mrid, 0.0)`): an implicit "treat as zero", forbidden by STD-REQ-3.
- A tie is skipped when `transferred > available` (strict), so equality closes; there is no tolerance.
- Shipped model, `CB-1201` open: isolation opens `SEC-SW-1201-1` and `REC-1201-2`; restoration re-closes `CB-1201`. Tie `TIE-1201-1405` has L = 1490 kW.
  - no capacity → tie skipped, note `"Hollow Creek tie to 1405 skipped: 1490 kW exceeds 0 kW available capacity"`, `customers_restored = 0`, `customers_remaining = 437`, `transferred_load_kw = 0.0`.
  - C = 1490.0 → tie closed, `customers_restored = 341`, `customers_remaining = 96`, `transferred_load_kw = 1490.0`, no notes.
  - C = 1489.5 → tie skipped (note says "1490 kW exceeds 1490 kW", rounding hides the 0.5 kW); C = 1489.4 → skipped.
  - C = NaN and C = +inf → tie **closed**, `customers_restored = 341`, no note.
- `build_plan` callers: `backend/app/api.py:45` and `backend/tests/test_flisr.py` only.
- HTTP today (`FlisrRequest`, Pydantic lax mode, extra fields ignored): a JSON `NaN` capacity is accepted, a string `"2000"` is coerced to 2000.0, and an unknown body field is silently ignored. All three reach the planner.
- No timestamp, no quality, no machine-readable reason for a skipped tie.

### Definitions

- **Candidate tie**: a `Switch` with `kind == tie` and `scada_controllable == True` for which `_nodes_restored_by` returns a non-empty node set. Other ties are skipped silently, as today (§3).
- **L (transferred load)**: sum of `Section.load_kw` over sections whose `to_node` is in the candidate node set. Unit kW; range L ≥ 0.
- **C (tie capacity)**: `TieCapacity.kw` — the alternate feeder's spare capacity as delivered by the SCADA scan every 10 s, kW on the same basis as `load_kw`. No unit conversion, no per-unit base, not nameplate (Q-SPEC-1).
- **τ (tolerance)**: 0.5 kW, the only tolerance; no additional safety margin (Q-SPEC-1, Q-SPEC-4). Per-unit statement waived by Q-SPEC-4.
- **as_of**: the evaluation instant, a timezone-aware instant. Over HTTP: the request's `as_of` (timezone-aware ISO-8601; a non-UTC offset is normalised to the same UTC instant), when absent the server's UTC now (Q-SPEC-10, Q-SPEC-12).
- **server now**: the server's UTC clock, read once when the HTTP request is handled; used only for the as_of bound (REQ-TIECAP-23) and for an absent as_of.
- **age**: `as_of − TieCapacity.timestamp`, in seconds (Q-SPEC-10). Negative when the timestamp is ahead of as_of.
- **Usable capacity**: an entry that is present, valid (REQ-TIECAP-8), `quality == "GOOD"` and `age ≤ 20 s` (Q-SPEC-2).
- **Request validation**: FastAPI/Pydantic validation of the `POST /flisr/plan` body; a failure returns HTTP 422 and the planner is not called, so no plan at all is produced (Q-SPEC-9, Q-SPEC-12).
- **Present** (HTTP body field): the key appears in the JSON body, whatever its value.

- `locate_fault` / fault-location logic; `_isolation_switches` and DEF-FLISR-7 (a tie that is an isolation point back-feeds the faulted section) — separate defect run. This change shall neither fix nor mask DEF-FLISR-7.

## 4. Verification notes for QA

- Independent oracle: QA-owned BFS over the test topology plus closed-form `L ≤ C + 0.5`, `age > 20`, `age < −2`, `quality == "GOOD"`, `math.isfinite(kw) and kw ≥ 0`, and the REQ-TIECAP-9 precedence. It must not import `app.network` or `app.flisr` helpers.

- Order of work (`.agents/skills/safety-critical-change/SKILL.md`): baseline → characterization (REQ-TIECAP-19, REQ-TIECAP-22) → failing reproductions (missing capacity read as 0 kW with no machine-readable reason; legacy NaN closes the tie) → minimal fix → invariant (REQ-TIECAP-21, ≥ 500 seeded cases).
- Design note (measured, pydantic 2.14.1 / fastapi 0.143.1): a model-wide `ConfigDict(strict=True)` makes FastAPI reject valid ISO-8601 strings for datetime fields (`datetime_type`), because the body is validated in Python mode. Strictness must be applied so REQ-TIECAP-1/13 hold: numbers and strings strict, datetimes parsed from ISO-8601 strings only.

artifacts.design:
# Design — FLISR restoration respects tie-switch capacity

Run: `feature-tie-capacity` · Stage: DESIGN · Attempt: 1 · Inputs: `specification.md` (attempt 4, complete), `units.json` (U1–U4)
Safety classification: **safety-critical** (STD-SAFETY-1). Protected path `backend/app/flisr.py`: two human reviewers (STD-GOV-6).
Status: **BLOCKED on Q-DESIGN-1** (§9). Everything below is complete; only §6.3 depends on the answer.

Baseline re-measured on `main` @ 5f6b471: `pytest backend -q` → 2 passed; `ruff check backend tools` → 1 pre-existing error in `tools/` (UP017), unrelated to this change.

## 1. Components and layers

Layer map (repo contract): `ui → api → logic → models`. No lower layer imports an upper one (STD-ARCH-3).

| Layer | Module | Change | Imports (allowed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| models | `backend/app/models.py` | New: constants, `IsoAwareDatetime`, `TieCapacity`, `TieBlockReason`, `BlockedTie`. Extended: `RestorationPlan`. | pydantic, stdlib only |
| logic | `backend/app/flisr.py` | New: `tie_capacity_verdict()` (the single capacity characteristic), `_legacy_to_tie_capacity()`, `_blocked_note()`. Changed: `build_plan()` signature and tie loop. `locate_fault`, `_isolation_switches`, `_nodes_restored_by` unchanged. | `.models`, `.network` (same layer, as today) |
| logic | `backend/app/network.py` | Unchanged (`load_on_nodes` keeps computing L). | `.models` |
| api | `backend/app/api.py` | Changed: `FlisrRequest`, `flisr_plan` route; new `server_now()` dependency, `_check_as_of_bound()`. | `.flisr`, `.models`, `.network` |
| ui | `console/**` | Unchanged (does not call `/flisr/plan`). | — |

Data flow (HTTP): JSON body → FastAPI/Pydantic request validation (`FlisrRequest`, `TieCapacity`) → `_check_as_of_bound(as_of, server_now)` → `flisr.build_plan(..., tie_capacity | tie_capacity_kw, as_of=resolved)` → per candidate tie `tie_capacity_verdict(entry, L, as_of)` → `RestorationPlan` (with `blocked_ties`, `as_of`, `deprecations`) → HTTP 200. Any validation failure → HTTP 422 and `build_plan` is never called.

## 2. Data models — `backend/app/models.py` (U2, extended in U3)

Models and constants only; no plant decision logic (STD-ARCH-1). The one validator function is a type parser (it decides whether an input *is* an ISO-8601 string), not a plant decision.

```python
# Tie-capacity characteristic parameters (single source; spec Q-SPEC-1/2/4/10/12)
TIE_CAPACITY_TOLERANCE_KW: Final = 0.5
TIE_CAPACITY_MAX_AGE = timedelta(seconds=20)        # age > 20 s  -> CAPACITY_STALE
TIE_CAPACITY_MAX_LEAD = timedelta(seconds=2)        # age < -2 s  -> CAPACITY_INVALID
AS_OF_MAX_LAG = timedelta(seconds=60)               # server_now - as_of > 60 s -> 422
AS_OF_MAX_LEAD = timedelta(seconds=2)               # as_of - server_now > 2 s  -> 422
TIE_CAPACITY_GOOD_QUALITY: Final = "GOOD"

def _require_iso_string(value):          # BeforeValidator
    datetime -> pass through (Python callers);
    str      -> datetime.fromisoformat(value)  (rejects "yesterday", "1790000000")
    other    -> ValueError  (JSON numbers, bool, null)
IsoAwareDatetime = Annotated[AwareDatetime, BeforeValidator(_require_iso_string)]

class TieCapacity(BaseModel):            # REQ-TIECAP-1
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    kw: StrictFloat                      # JSON number only; NaN/±inf/negative pass (flagged by the planner)
    timestamp: IsoAwareDatetime          # aware ISO-8601 only; no clock comparison here
    quality: StrictStr

class TieBlockReason(StrEnum):           # REQ-TIECAP-11; declaration order == precedence (REQ-TIECAP-9)
    CAPACITY_INVALID, CAPACITY_UNKNOWN, CAPACITY_STALE, CAPACITY_EXCEEDED

class BlockedTie(BaseModel):
    tie_id: str
    reason: TieBlockReason

class RestorationPlan(BaseModel):        # existing fields unchanged
    ...
    as_of: AwareDatetime                 # U3, REQ-TIECAP-14: required, always UTC
    blocked_ties: list[BlockedTie] = []  # U2, REQ-TIECAP-11
    deprecations: list[str] = []         # U3, REQ-TIECAP-16
```

Why per-field strictness, not `ConfigDict(strict=True)`: measured on pydantic 2.14.1 / fastapi 0.143.1 (this stage, prototype outside the repo), FastAPI validates the body in Python mode, so model-wide strict rejects valid ISO strings (`datetime_type`), and lax `AwareDatetime` alone accepts the numeric string `"1790000000"` as a Unix time. `IsoAwareDatetime` measured: `"yesterday"`, `1790000000`, `"1790000000"`, `null`, naive and date-only → rejected; `Z`, `+02:00`, basic `20261015T220000Z` → accepted. `StrictFloat` measured: JSON `2000` → 2000.0 accepted; `"2000"`, `true`, `null` → rejected; JSON `NaN`/`-Infinity` reach the model. `extra="forbid"` → `extra_forbidden` 422.

`RestorationPlan.as_of` is required because REQ-TIECAP-14 says *always*; `flisr.build_plan` is the only constructor (grep: `flisr.py:76`). Characterization (U1) pins fields individually, so it is unaffected.

## 3. Shared characteristic — `flisr.tie_capacity_verdict` (STD-ARCH-2)

One implementation of the capacity decision, used by `build_plan` and by nothing else in production:

```python
def tie_capacity_verdict(
    entry: TieCapacity | None, transferred_kw: float, as_of: datetime
) -> TieBlockReason | None:
    """None = the tie may close. Otherwise the first applicable reason (REQ-TIECAP-9).
    Absent entry -> CAPACITY_UNKNOWN. Out-of-range kw (NaN, ±inf, < 0) or timestamp more than
    2 s ahead of as_of -> CAPACITY_INVALID. Non-GOOD quality -> CAPACITY_UNKNOWN. Older than
    20 s -> CAPACITY_STALE. Never substitutes or clamps a value."""
    if entry is None:                                          -> CAPACITY_UNKNOWN
    age = as_of - entry.timestamp                              # timedelta, exact µs
    if not (math.isfinite(entry.kw) and entry.kw >= 0.0) or age < -TIE_CAPACITY_MAX_LEAD:
                                                               -> CAPACITY_INVALID
    if entry.quality != TIE_CAPACITY_GOOD_QUALITY:             -> CAPACITY_UNKNOWN
    if age > TIE_CAPACITY_MAX_AGE:                             -> CAPACITY_STALE
    if transferred_kw <= entry.kw + TIE_CAPACITY_TOLERANCE_KW: -> None (close)
    return CAPACITY_EXCEEDED
```

Design decisions:
- **Positive close condition.** The tie closes only when `L <= C + τ` evaluates True. Any NaN that reaches the comparison (e.g. a NaN `Section.load_kw` in the model file) evaluates False and blocks. Today's `transferred > available` closes on NaN (spec intended change 3); this structure removes that failure mode rather than special-casing it (STD-SAFETY-4).
- **Ages compared as `timedelta`**, never as float seconds, so the 20.000 s / 20.001 s and −2.000 s / −2.001 s boundaries are exact at microsecond resolution (measured: `20.001 s > 20 s` True, `20 s > 20 s` False).
- `kw = -0.0` passes `>= 0.0` (valid, as the spec requires).
- Precedence is the order of the `if` statements; a missing entry can only be UNKNOWN.

## 4. Planner — `flisr.build_plan` (U3)

```python
def build_plan(
    feeder: Feeder,
    lockout_switch_mrid: str,
    tie_capacity_kw: dict[str, float] | None = None,     # legacy, deprecated (kept positional for callers)
    *,
    tie_capacity: dict[str, TieCapacity] | None = None,
    as_of: datetime | None = None,
) -> RestorationPlan:
```

Behaviour for absent / stale / out-of-range inputs (STD-ARCH-4), in docstring form:

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| both `tie_capacity` and `tie_capacity_kw` not None (incl. both `{}`) | `ValueError`; no plan (REQ-TIECAP-15) |
| `as_of` None | `datetime.now(UTC)` read **once** at entry (REQ-TIECAP-2, REQ-TIECAP-20) |
| `as_of` naive | `ValueError`; no plan (REQ-TIECAP-2) |
| `as_of` aware, any offset | `as_of.astimezone(UTC)`; same instant; stored in `plan.as_of` |
| `tie_capacity_kw` given (legacy) | each entry → `TieCapacity.model_construct(kw=float(v), timestamp=as_of, quality="GOOD")` (no re-validation, so NaN/±inf/negative survive and become CAPACITY_INVALID); `plan.deprecations = ["tie_capacity_kw"]` (REQ-TIECAP-16) |
| both None, or `{}` | every candidate tie CAPACITY_UNKNOWN (REQ-TIECAP-5) |
| entry for a non-candidate tie | ignored, as today (spec §3) |
| lockout not open / no isolating switch | `FlisrError`, unchanged |
| no fault indication | unchanged early return; `blocked_ties` stays `[]` (REQ-TIECAP-19) |

Why `ValueError` and not `FlisrError`: `FlisrError` means "the network state does not allow a defensible plan" and maps to HTTP 409. Naive `as_of` and both-maps are caller contract violations that HTTP validation already rejects with 422, so they never reach `build_plan` from `api.py`; a direct Python caller gets an exception and no plan either way.

Tie loop (replaces `flisr.py:92-121`; isolation, lockout re-close and `_nodes_restored_by` untouched, REQ-TIECAP-10):

```text
for switch in feeder.switches:                 # order => blocked_ties order (REQ-TIECAP-11)
    skip silently if not tie / not SCADA / empty candidate set     # as today
    L = load_on_nodes(feeder, candidate_nodes)
    customers = Σ customers of sections whose to_node ∈ candidate_nodes
    entry = capacities.get(switch.mrid)       # no default value — removes `.get(..., 0.0)` at flisr.py:98
    reason = tie_capacity_verdict(entry, L, as_of)
    if reason is None:
        append close step; transferred_load_kw += L; customers_restored += customers   # unchanged
    else:
        blocked_ties.append(BlockedTie(tie_id=switch.mrid, reason=reason))
        notes.append(_blocked_note(switch, reason, entry, L, as_of))
        customers_remaining += customers                                        # REQ-TIECAP-18
```

Operator notes (`_blocked_note`, REQ-TIECAP-12), one per blocked tie, naming `Switch.name` and the reason code:

| Reason | Note |
|---|---|
| CAPACITY_EXCEEDED | `"{name} blocked (CAPACITY_EXCEEDED): {L:.1f} kW to transfer exceeds {C:.1f} kW available capacity (+0.5 kW tolerance)"` |
| CAPACITY_STALE | `"{name} blocked (CAPACITY_STALE): capacity value is {age_s:.3f} s old (limit 20 s)"` |
| CAPACITY_UNKNOWN | `"{name} blocked (CAPACITY_UNKNOWN): no capacity value"` or `"...: capacity quality {quality!r} is not GOOD"` |
| CAPACITY_INVALID | `"{name} blocked (CAPACITY_INVALID): capacity {kw} kW is not a finite non-negative number"` or `"...: capacity timestamp is {lead_s:.3f} s ahead of as_of (limit 2 s)"` |

Error handling removed and its replacement in the same change (STD-ARCH-5):

| Removed | Replacement |
|---|---|
| `tie_capacity_kw = tie_capacity_kw or {}` + `.get(mrid, 0.0)` (implicit zero) | explicit `entry = None` → CAPACITY_UNKNOWN, machine-readable |
| `transferred > available` skip guard | `tie_capacity_verdict` positive close condition (blocks NaN that the old guard let through) |
| free-text-only skip note | `blocked_ties` entry + note |

## 5. Endpoint — `POST /flisr/plan` in `backend/app/api.py` (U3)

`FlisrRequest` stays in `api.py` (existing convention for HTTP request schemas: `EstimationRequest`, `AgcRequest`). It is an API-layer DTO, not a domain model; it reuses `TieCapacity` and `IsoAwareDatetime` from `models.py`.

```python
class FlisrRequest(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")                    # unknown body field -> 422
    feeder_mrid: StrictStr
    lockout_switch_mrid: StrictStr
    tie_capacity: dict[str, TieCapacity] | None = None
    tie_capacity_kw: dict[str, StrictFloat] | None = None        # deprecated
    as_of: IsoAwareDatetime | None = None

    @field_validator("tie_capacity", "tie_capacity_kw", "as_of", mode="before")
    def _no_null(v): None -> ValueError("omit the field instead of sending null")   # defaults are not validated, so "absent" still works
    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _mutually_exclusive(self): both not None -> ValueError   # REQ-TIECAP-15 (both {} included)

def server_now() -> datetime:          # FastAPI dependency; tests override via app.dependency_overrides
    return datetime.now(UTC)

def _check_as_of_bound(as_of, now):    # REQ-TIECAP-23; raises RequestValidationError(loc=("body","as_of")) -> 422
    now - as_of > AS_OF_MAX_LAG  or  as_of - now > AS_OF_MAX_LEAD  -> reject   (exactly 60 s / 2 s accepted)

@router.post("/flisr/plan", response_model=RestorationPlan, description=<deprecation + mutual-exclusion note>)
def flisr_plan(request: FlisrRequest, now: datetime = Depends(server_now)) -> RestorationPlan:
    as_of = request.as_of if request.as_of is not None else now     # server clock read once per request
    _check_as_of_bound(as_of, now)                                  # before load_network / build_plan
    ... flisr.build_plan(feeder, lockout, request.tie_capacity_kw,
                         tie_capacity=request.tie_capacity, as_of=as_of)
    KeyError -> 404, FlisrError -> 409   (unchanged); blocked ties -> 200 (REQ-TIECAP-13)
```

Prototype measurements (pydantic 2.14.1 / fastapi 0.143.1, outside the repo): `"kw":"2000"`, `true`, `null` → 422 `float_type`; timestamp `"yesterday"`, `1790000000` → 422; naive → 422 `timezone_aware`; extra field at body and `TieCapacity` level → 422 `extra_forbidden`; `"tie_capacity": null` and `"as_of": null` → 422; both maps `{}` → 422; JSON `NaN` / `-Infinity` → reaches handler (planner then CAPACITY_INVALID); `RequestValidationError` raised in the handler → standard 422 body; the response serialises a UTC `as_of` as `...Z`.

OpenAPI `description` (REQ-TIECAP-17): "`tie_capacity_kw` is deprecated and will be removed one release after this one. It is mutually exclusive with `tie_capacity`; sending both returns 422. Legacy values are treated as quality GOOD with timestamp = as_of." Not `Field(deprecated=True)`: in pydantic 2.14 that emits a `DeprecationWarning` whenever the handler reads the attribute.

## 1. Components and layers

| models | `backend/app/models.py` | New: constants, `IsoAwareDatetime`, `TieCapacity`, `TieBlockReason`, `BlockedTie`. Extended: `RestorationPlan`. | pydantic, stdlib only |

Changed: `build_plan()` signature and tie loop. `locate_fault`, `_isolation_switches`, `_nodes_restored_by` unchanged. | `.models`, `.network` (same layer, as today) |

Data flow (HTTP): JSON body → FastAPI/Pydantic request validation (`FlisrRequest`, `TieCapacity`) → `_check_as_of_bound(as_of, server_now)` → `flisr.build_plan(..., tie_capacity | tie_capacity_kw, as_of=resolved)` → per candidate tie `tie_capacity_verdict(entry, L, as_of)` → `RestorationPlan` (with `blocked_ties`, `as_of`, `deprecations`) → HTTP 200. Any validation failure → HTTP 422 and `build_plan` is never called.

## 2. Data models — `backend/app/models.py` (U2, extended in U3)

U2 adds the characteristic constants, `IsoAwareDatetime`, `TieCapacity`, `TieBlockReason`, `BlockedTie` and `RestorationPlan.blocked_ties`, all additive. U3 adds only `RestorationPlan.as_of` and `RestorationPlan.deprecations` (units.json U3 scope note).

Models and constants only; no plant decision logic (STD-ARCH-1). The one validator function is a type parser (it decides whether an input *is* an ISO-8601 string), not a plant decision.

```python
# Tie-capacity characteristic parameters: the ONE production source (STD-ARCH-1/2, Q-DESIGN-1).
# Imported by flisr.tie_capacity_verdict, flisr._blocked_note, api._check_as_of_bound and the
# /flisr/plan OpenAPI description. No production module restates these values (spec Q-SPEC-1/2/4/10/12).
TIE_CAPACITY_TOLERANCE_KW: Final = 0.5
TIE_CAPACITY_MAX_AGE = timedelta(seconds=20)        # age > 20 s  -> CAPACITY_STALE
TIE_CAPACITY_MAX_LEAD = timedelta(seconds=2)        # age < -2 s  -> CAPACITY_INVALID
AS_OF_MAX_LAG = timedelta(seconds=60)               # server_now - as_of > 60 s -> 422
AS_OF_MAX_LEAD = timedelta(seconds=2)               # as_of - server_now > 2 s  -> 422
TIE_CAPACITY_GOOD_QUALITY: Final = "GOOD"

def _require_iso_string(value):          # BeforeValidator
    datetime -> pass through (Python callers);
    str      -> datetime.fromisoformat(value)  (rejects "yesterday", "1790000000")
    other    -> ValueError  (JSON numbers, bool, null)
IsoAwareDatetime = Annotated[AwareDatetime, BeforeValidator(_require_iso_string)]

class TieCapacity(BaseModel):            # REQ-TIECAP-1
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
    kw: StrictFloat                      # JSON number only; NaN/±inf/negative pass (flagged by the planner)
    timestamp: IsoAwareDatetime          # aware ISO-8601 only; no clock comparison here
    quality: StrictStr

class TieBlockReason(StrEnum):           # REQ-TIECAP-11; declaration order == precedence (REQ-TIECAP-9)
    CAPACITY_INVALID, CAPACITY_UNKNOWN, CAPACITY_STALE, CAPACITY_EXCEEDED

class BlockedTie(BaseModel):
    tie_id: str
    reason: TieBlockReason

class RestorationPlan(BaseModel):        # existing fields unchanged
    ...
    as_of: AwareDatetime                 # U3, REQ-TIECAP-14: required, always UTC
    blocked_ties: list[BlockedTie] = []  # U2, REQ-TIECAP-11
    deprecations: list[str] = []         # U3, REQ-TIECAP-16
```

Why per-field strictness, not `ConfigDict(strict=True)`: measured on pydantic 2.14.1 / fastapi 0.143.1 (this stage, prototype outside the repo), FastAPI validates the body in Python mode, so model-wide strict rejects valid ISO strings (`datetime_type`), and lax `AwareDatetime` alone accepts the numeric string `"1790000000"` as a Unix time. `IsoAwareDatetime` measured: `"yesterday"`, `1790000000`, `"1790000000"`, `null`, naive and date-only → rejected; `Z`, `+02:00`, basic `20261015T220000Z` → accepted. `StrictFloat` measured: JSON `2000` → 2000.0 accepted; `"2000"`, `true`, `null` → rejected; JSON `NaN`/`-Infinity` reach the model. `extra="forbid"` → `extra_forbidden` 422.

`RestorationPlan.as_of` is required because REQ-TIECAP-14 says *always*; `flisr.build_plan` is the only constructor (grep: `flisr.py:76`). Characterization (U1) pins fields individually, so it is unaffected.

## 3. Shared characteristic — `flisr.tie_capacity_verdict` (STD-ARCH-2)

There is one implementation of the capacity decision. Its parameters come only from the `models.py` constants in §2. Production consumers (Q-DESIGN-1):

| Consumer | Uses |
|---|---|
| `flisr.build_plan` tie loop (planner) | calls `tie_capacity_verdict`; no comparison of its own |
| `flisr._blocked_note` (operator notes) | formats `TIE_CAPACITY_TOLERANCE_KW`, `TIE_CAPACITY_MAX_AGE`, `TIE_CAPACITY_MAX_LEAD`; never re-derives the reason, only formats the reason the verdict returned |
| `api._check_as_of_bound` (endpoint) | `AS_OF_MAX_LAG`, `AS_OF_MAX_LEAD` |
| `api` route `description` (OpenAPI) | formats the same constants into the deprecation note |

No production module other than `models.py` contains the literals 0.5, 20, 2 or 60 for these purposes. A test enforces this (§6.3, check P2).

```python
def tie_capacity_verdict(
    entry: TieCapacity | None, transferred_kw: float, as_of: datetime
) -> TieBlockReason | None:
    """None = the tie may close. Otherwise the first applicable reason (REQ-TIECAP-9).
    Absent entry -> CAPACITY_UNKNOWN. Out-of-range kw (NaN, ±inf, < 0) or timestamp more than
    2 s ahead of as_of -> CAPACITY_INVALID. Non-GOOD quality -> CAPACITY_UNKNOWN. Older than
    20 s -> CAPACITY_STALE. Never substitutes or clamps a value."""
    if entry is None:                                          -> CAPACITY_UNKNOWN
    age = as_of - entry.timestamp                              # timedelta, exact µs
    if _kw_invalid(entry.kw) or age < -TIE_CAPACITY_MAX_LEAD:   # _kw_invalid: not (isfinite(kw) and kw >= 0.0)
                                                               -> CAPACITY_INVALID
    if entry.quality != TIE_CAPACITY_GOOD_QUALITY:             -> CAPACITY_UNKNOWN
    if age > TIE_CAPACITY_MAX_AGE:                             -> CAPACITY_STALE
    if transferred_kw <= entry.kw + TIE_CAPACITY_TOLERANCE_KW: -> None (close)
    return CAPACITY_EXCEEDED
```

Design decisions:
- **Positive close condition.** The tie closes only when `L <= C + τ` evaluates True. Any NaN that reaches the comparison (e.g. a NaN `Section.load_kw` in the model file) evaluates False and blocks. Today's `transferred > available` closes on NaN (spec intended change 3); this structure removes that failure mode rather than special-casing it (STD-SAFETY-4).
- **Ages compared as `timedelta`**, never as float seconds, so the 20.000 s / 20.001 s and −2.000 s / −2.001 s boundaries are exact at microsecond resolution (measured: `20.001 s > 20 s` True, `20 s > 20 s` False).
- `kw = -0.0` passes `>= 0.0` (valid, as the spec requires).
- Precedence is the order of the `if` statements; a missing entry can only be UNKNOWN.

## 4. Planner — `flisr.build_plan` (U3)

```python
def build_plan(
    feeder: Feeder,
    lockout_switch_mrid: str,
    tie_capacity_kw: dict[str, float] | None = None,     # legacy, deprecated (kept positional for callers)
    *,
    tie_capacity: dict[str, TieCapacity] | None = None,
    as_of: datetime | None = None,
) -> RestorationPlan:
```

Behaviour for absent / stale / out-of-range inputs (STD-ARCH-4), in docstring form:

| Input | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| both `tie_capacity` and `tie_capacity_kw` not None (incl. both `{}`) | `ValueError`; no plan (REQ-TIECAP-15) |
| `as_of` None | `datetime.now(UTC)` read **once** at entry (REQ-TIECAP-2, REQ-TIECAP-20) |
| `as_of` naive | `ValueError`; no plan (REQ-TIECAP-2) |
| `as_of` aware, any offset | `as_of.astimezone(UTC)`; same instant; stored in `plan.as_of` |
| `tie_capacity_kw` given (legacy) | each entry → `TieCapacity.model_construct(kw=float(v), timestamp=as_of, quality="GOOD")` (no re-validation, so NaN/±inf/negative survive and become CAPACITY_INVALID); `plan.deprecations = ["tie_capacity_kw"]` (REQ-TIECAP-16) |
| both None, or `{}` | every candidate tie CAPACITY_UNKNOWN (REQ-TIECAP-5) |
| entry for a non-candidate tie | ignored, as today (spec §3) |
| lockout not open / no isolating switch | `FlisrError`, unchanged |
| no fault indication | unchanged early return; `blocked_ties` stays `[]` (REQ-TIECAP-19) |

Why `ValueError` and not `FlisrError`: `FlisrError` means "the network state does not allow a defensible plan" and maps to HTTP 409. Naive `as_of` and both-maps are caller contract violations that HTTP validation already rejects with 422, so they never reach `build_plan` from `api.py`; a direct Python caller gets an exception and no plan either way.

Tie loop (replaces `flisr.py:92-121`; isolation, lockout re-close and `_nodes_restored_by` untouched, REQ-TIECAP-10):

```text
for switch in feeder.switches:                 # order => blocked_ties order (REQ-TIECAP-11)
    skip silently if not tie / not SCADA / empty candidate set     # as today
    L = load_on_nodes(feeder, candidate_nodes)
    customers = Σ customers of sections whose to_node ∈ candidate_nodes
    entry = capacities.get(switch.mrid)       # no default value — removes `.get(..., 0.0)` at flisr.py:98
    reason = tie_capacity_verdict(entry, L, as_of)
    if reason is None:
        append close step; transferred_load_kw += L; customers_restored += customers   # unchanged
    else:
        blocked_ties.append(BlockedTie(tie_id=switch.mrid, reason=reason))
        notes.append(_blocked_note(switch, reason, entry, L, as_of))
        customers_remaining += customers                                        # REQ-TIECAP-18
```

Operator notes (`_blocked_note`, REQ-TIECAP-12), one per blocked tie, naming `Switch.name` and the reason code:

| Reason | Note |
|---|---|
| CAPACITY_EXCEEDED | `"{name} blocked (CAPACITY_EXCEEDED): {L:.1f} kW to transfer exceeds {C:.1f} kW available capacity (+{TIE_CAPACITY_TOLERANCE_KW:g} kW tolerance)"` |
| CAPACITY_STALE | `"{name} blocked (CAPACITY_STALE): capacity value is {age_s:.3f} s old (limit {TIE_CAPACITY_MAX_AGE.total_seconds():g} s)"` |
| CAPACITY_UNKNOWN | `"{name} blocked (CAPACITY_UNKNOWN): no capacity value"` or `"...: capacity quality {quality!r} is not GOOD"` |
| CAPACITY_INVALID | `"{name} blocked (CAPACITY_INVALID): capacity {kw} kW is not a finite non-negative number"` or `"...: capacity timestamp is {lead_s:.3f} s ahead of as_of (limit {TIE_CAPACITY_MAX_LEAD.total_seconds():g} s)"` |

Rendered on the shipped model these read, for example, `+0.5 kW tolerance`, `limit 20 s`, `limit 2 s`. The limit text comes from the same constants the verdict uses, so a note can never state a limit different from the one applied. `_blocked_note` receives the reason from `tie_capacity_verdict` and does not compare anything itself. For UNKNOWN and INVALID it chooses between the two message variants with presence and type checks only (entry is None or not; which INVALID sub-condition holds). Those sub-condition checks reuse the verdict's predicates through a private helper `_kw_invalid(kw)` in `flisr.py`; they are not re-implemented.

Error handling removed and its replacement in the same change (STD-ARCH-5):

| Removed | Replacement |
|---|---|
| `tie_capacity_kw = tie_capacity_kw or {}` + `.get(mrid, 0.0)` (implicit zero) | explicit `entry = None` → CAPACITY_UNKNOWN, machine-readable |
| `transferred > available` skip guard | `tie_capacity_verdict` positive close condition (blocks NaN that the old guard let through) |
| free-text-only skip note | `blocked_ties` entry + note |

## 5. Endpoint — `POST /flisr/plan` in `backend/app/api.py` (U3)

`FlisrRequest` stays in `api.py` (existing convention for HTTP request schemas: `EstimationRequest`, `AgcRequest`). It is an API-layer DTO, not a domain model; it reuses `TieCapacity` and `IsoAwareDatetime` from `models.py`.

```python
class FlisrRequest(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")                    # unknown body field -> 422
    feeder_mrid: StrictStr
    lockout_switch_mrid: StrictStr
    tie_capacity: dict[str, TieCapacity] | None = None
    tie_capacity_kw: dict[str, StrictFloat] | None = None        # deprecated
    as_of: IsoAwareDatetime | None = None

    @field_validator("tie_capacity", "tie_capacity_kw", "as_of", mode="before")
    def _no_null(v): None -> ValueError("omit the field instead of sending null")   # defaults are not validated, so "absent" still works
    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _mutually_exclusive(self): both not None -> ValueError   # REQ-TIECAP-15 (both {} included)

def server_now() -> datetime:          # FastAPI dependency; tests override via app.dependency_overrides
    return datetime.now(UTC)

def _check_as_of_bound(as_of, now):    # REQ-TIECAP-23; raises RequestValidationError(loc=("body","as_of")) -> 422
    now - as_of > AS_OF_MAX_LAG  or  as_of - now > AS_OF_MAX_LEAD  -> reject   (exactly 60 s / 2 s accepted)

@router.post("/flisr/plan", response_model=RestorationPlan, description=<deprecation + mutual-exclusion note>)
def flisr_plan(request: FlisrRequest, now: datetime = Depends(server_now)) -> RestorationPlan:
    as_of = request.as_of if request.as_of is not None else now     # server clock read once per request
    _check_as_of_bound(as_of, now)                                  # before load_network / build_plan
    ... flisr.build_plan(feeder, lockout, request.tie_capacity_kw,
                         tie_capacity=request.tie_capacity, as_of=as_of)
    KeyError -> 404, FlisrError -> 409   (unchanged); blocked ties -> 200 (REQ-TIECAP-13)
```

Prototype measurements (pydantic 2.14.1 / fastapi 0.143.1, outside the repo): `"kw":"2000"`, `true`, `null` → 422 `float_type`; timestamp `"yesterday"`, `1790000000` → 422; naive → 422 `timezone_aware`; extra field at body and `TieCapacity` level → 422 `extra_forbidden`; `"tie_capacity": null` and `"as_of": null` → 422; both maps `{}` → 422; JSON `NaN` / `-Infinity` → reaches handler (planner then CAPACITY_INVALID); `RequestValidationError` raised in the handler → standard 422 body; the response serialises a UTC `as_of` as `...Z`.

OpenAPI `description` (REQ-TIECAP-17), a module-level string in `api.py` built from the `models.py` constants (for example the 0.5 kW tolerance and the 20 s / 2 s limits) so it cannot drift from them: "`tie_capacity_kw` is deprecated and will be removed one release after this one. It is mutually exclusive with `tie_capacity`; sending both returns 422. Legacy values are treated as quality GOOD with timestamp = as_of." Not `Field(deprecated=True)`: in pydantic 2.14 that emits a `DeprecationWarning` whenever the handler reads the attribute.

### 6.3 Oracle and the scoped STD-ARCH-2 waiver (Q-DESIGN-1)

**Waiver (explicit and scoped).** STD-ARCH-2 says one shared implementation of a numerically sensitive characteristic is used by every consumer, test oracle included, and calls duplicates a VIOLATION. STD-SAFETY-6 requires operate boundaries to be checked against an *independent* closed-form oracle. Per Q-DESIGN-1 (principal-engineer-standin), **STD-SAFETY-6 governs the test oracle** and **STD-ARCH-2 applies to production consumers only** (planner, endpoint, notes; §3). Scope of the waiver:

- Covers only the QA oracle functions in `backend/tests/test_flisr_tie_capacity_planner.py`, `test_flisr_tie_capacity_api.py` and `test_flisr_tie_capacity_invariant.py`, which restate the closed forms below.
- Does not cover any module under `backend/app/`. A second production implementation of the characteristic, or a restated production literal, is still a STD-ARCH-2 VIOLATION.
- The U3 and U4 oracles are separate restatements: units.json says U4's oracle is "implemented in the test file". Both use the literals from the specification. Under the waiver this is intended: more diversity, no shared defect.

**Oracle content.** The oracle lives under `backend/tests`. It does not import `app.flisr` or `app.network` and does not use the `models.py` threshold constants (Q-DESIGN-1: "must not import app.flisr or share its threshold code"). It may read `app.models` data types (`Feeder`, `Section`, `Switch`, `TieCapacity`) as plain data. Functions are named `oracle_*`:

| Oracle function | Closed form (literals from the specification) |
|---|---|
| `oracle_candidate_nodes(feeder, tie_mrid, opened)` | its own BFS over the test topology: nodes reachable from the tie's `from_node` with isolation switches open and the tie closed, minus nodes reachable from `source_node` (spec "Candidate tie" definition) |
| `oracle_load_kw(feeder, nodes)` / `oracle_customers(...)` | Σ `load_kw` / `customers` of sections whose `to_node` ∈ nodes |
| `oracle_reason(entry, L, as_of)` | `None` → UNKNOWN; `not (isfinite(kw) and kw >= 0) or age < timedelta(seconds=-2)` → INVALID; `quality != "GOOD"` → UNKNOWN; `age > timedelta(seconds=20)` → STALE; `L <= kw + 0.5` → close; else EXCEEDED (REQ-TIECAP-9 precedence) |
| `oracle_as_of_ok(as_of, now)` (API test) | `now - as_of <= timedelta(seconds=60) and as_of - now <= timedelta(seconds=2)` |

Tolerance: 0.5 kW in engineering units. Per-unit statement waived by Q-SPEC-4; the PR records this waiver against STD-SAFETY-6.

**Checks that keep the oracle independent and the production source single** (all in the U2/U3/U4 files already listed in units.json; no new files):

- **O1 — oracle independence** (planner, API and invariant test files): an `ast` check of the test module asserts that no `oracle_*` function refers to a name bound by `from app.flisr …`, `from app.network …`, `import app.flisr` / `app.network`, or to a `models.TIE_CAPACITY_*` / `models.AS_OF_*` constant. The module may import `build_plan` / the app as the subject under test; only the oracle functions are constrained.
- **P1 — constant pin** (U2, `test_flisr_tie_capacity_models.py`): asserts `TIE_CAPACITY_TOLERANCE_KW == 0.5`, `TIE_CAPACITY_MAX_AGE == timedelta(seconds=20)`, `TIE_CAPACITY_MAX_LEAD == timedelta(seconds=2)`, `AS_OF_MAX_LAG == timedelta(seconds=60)`, `AS_OF_MAX_LEAD == timedelta(seconds=2)`, `TIE_CAPACITY_GOOD_QUALITY == "GOOD"`, using spec literals. A wrong constant then fails a test; the oracle does not move with it.
- **P2 — no restated production literal** (U3, planner test): an `ast` check of `tie_capacity_verdict`, `_kw_invalid`, `_blocked_note` (from `app/flisr.py` source) and `_check_as_of_bound` plus the route description builder (from `app/api.py` source) asserts no numeric constant other than `0` / `0.0` and no `timedelta(...)` call. This mechanically enforces §3's single production source.
- **Oracle self-check** (planner test): the oracle reproduces the §6.2 hand-computed shipped-model values (L = 1490.0 kW, 341 customers, the boundary verdicts) before it is used against `build_plan`.

questions.question: A section with negative Section.load_kw (e.g. DG export) inside a candidate set whose total L is still >= 0 makes L understate the load the tie would actually carry (measured: spur -600 kW, C=1000 -> closes at L=890 kW while the non-negative loads total 1490 kW). Pick one: (a) refuse the plan with FlisrError when any candidate-section load_kw < 0 (recommended; REQ-TIECAP-3/21 scoped to non-negative section loads); (b) use gross L = sum(max(load_kw, 0)) (changes the spec's L definition); (c) keep REQ-TIECAP-3 literal and accept the residual risk; (d) declare negative loads out of scope (model-team rule, no runtime check).
